checklist_item.title: Verify Fork Digest Computation: Is compute_fork_digest correctly implemented to derive the expected digest for each epoch?

reachability.notes: A P2P peer can send blocks with arbitrary fork digests. If fork digest validation is missing, blocks from different fork versions could be processed as if they belong to the current fork.

Confirm the genesis validators root is correctly incorporated into the digest computation. 4. Test with known test vectors: compute digest for pre-fork epoch, at-fork epoch, and post-fork epoch. 5. Verify the function handles epoch boundary conditions correctly (e.g., exact fork epoch transition).
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-50, Element: SG-003. Internal verification that the fork digest computation is correct, as incorrect computation would allow fork confusion attacks.

phase1.summary: ComputeForkDigest correctly implements the Ethereum specification for fork digest computation. It computes ForkData by SSZ hashing the ForkData structure containing version and genesisValidatorsRoot, then returns the first 4 bytes as per spec.
phase1.abstract_state_space: Input domain: (version: []byte, genesisValidatorsRoot: []byte) -> Output: ([4]byte, error). The function constructs ForkData{CurrentVersion: version, GenesisValidatorsRoot: root}, computes HashTreeRoot via SSZ serialization, applies bytesutil.ToBytes4 to extract first 4 bytes. Caching layer via digestMap reduces recomputation overhead.

phase2.symbolic_constraints: Success path: version and genesisValidatorsRoot are valid byte slices -> computeForkDataRoot succeeds with cached or computed SSZ hash -> ToBytes4 extracts bytes [0:4]. Error path: SSZ HashTreeRoot fails (malformed input, but this is protected by type system for well-formed ForkData struct).

phase3.proof_sketch: The implementation follows Ethereum consensus spec verbatim: compute_fork_digest(current_version, genesis_validators_root) = ForkDigest(compute_fork_data_root(current_version, genesis_validators_root)[:4]). Line 277-280 creates ForkData structure with CurrentVersion and GenesisValidatorsRoot fields, calls HashTreeRoot() which is SSZ-deterministic. Line 309 applies bytesutil.ToBytes4 which safely extracts first 4 bytes. Caching (lines 271-276, 287-289) is thread-safe with RWMutex. No tampering risk as cryptographic hash ensures integrity.
phase3.severity_assessment: No vulnerability detected. Implementation is cryptographically sound and matches specification. Caching provides performance benefit without introducing race conditions.

phase1.summary: The CL implements timeout handling for Engine API calls. Both NewPayload and ForkchoiceUpdated set context deadlines using ExecutionEngineTimeoutValue (default 8 seconds per Ethereum spec). SYNCING status returns ErrAcceptedSyncingPayloadStatus error which is handled upstream.
phase1.abstract_state_space: NewPayload and ForkchoiceUpdated create context with deadline at time.Now() + ExecutionEngineTimeoutValue seconds. If EL returns SYNCING, error ErrAcceptedSyncingPayloadStatus propagates. State transitions: (1) Call initiated with timeout, (2) RPC call to EL, (3) Response handling: SYNCING -> error return, VALID -> success, timeout -> ErrHTTPTimeout.

phase2.symbolic_constraints: Timeout condition: EL response time > ExecutionEngineTimeoutValue (8s). SYNCING status: lines 193-194 (NewPayload) and 263-264 (ForkchoiceUpdated) return ErrAcceptedSyncingPayloadStatus when pb.PayloadStatus_SYNCING or pb.PayloadStatus_ACCEPTED received. Context deadline enforced at lines 152-154 (NewPayload) and 215-217 (ForkchoiceUpdated).

phase3.proof_sketch: Lines 152-154 in NewPayload: context.WithDeadline(ctx, time.Now() + ExecutionEngineTimeoutValue*time.Second) ensures timeout. Lines 215-217 in ForkchoiceUpdated: identical pattern. SYNCING handling at lines 193-194 and 263-264 converts EL SYNCING status to error, preventing indefinite blocking. handleRPCError (lines 808-809) converts timeout errors to ErrHTTPTimeout. Invariant: No Engine API call blocks indefinitely; all have 8-second deadline.
phase3.severity_assessment: Trust boundary integrity maintained. Timeout handling prevents DoS from unresponsive EL. SYNCING status properly propagated as error for upstream handling.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005/tb-009: Is the proposer deterministically identifiable and cryptographically bound to each slot?

phase1.summary: Proposer index is deterministically computed via BeaconProposerIndex (lines 260-372 in validators.go) using cryptographic seed derived from state, epoch, and slot. Proposer is cryptographically bound to block via signature verification. No repudiation risk detected.
phase1.abstract_state_space: Proposer selection: seed = Hash(Seed(state, epoch, DomainBeaconProposer) + slot_bytes) (line 363-364). Active validator indices shuffled deterministically (ComputeProposerIndex lines 398-441). Same inputs always produce same proposer index. Cryptographic binding: Block signature verification in signing_root.go (VerifyBlockSigningRoot lines 174-193) ensures only proposer's private key can sign valid block for slot.

phase2.symbolic_constraints: Proposer index computation path: (1) BeaconProposerIndexAtSlot called with state and slot (line 322), (2) Seed computed from state.randao_mixes, epoch, DomainBeaconProposer (line 358), (3) seedWithSlot = Seed + slot_bytes (line 363), (4) seedWithSlotHash = Hash(seedWithSlot) (line 364), (5) ComputeProposerIndex selects from active validators using weighted sampling by effective balance (lines 398-441). Determinism: Same state + slot always yields same seed, same hash, same proposer. Non-repudiation: Block proposer must sign with BLS key; VerifyBlockSigningRoot (line 175-192) checks signature against proposer public key.

phase3.proof_sketch: Determinism proof: Lines 358-364 show seed derivation is pure function of state (randao_mixes, validators) and slot. Hash function (line 364) is deterministic. ComputeProposerIndex (lines 398-441) uses deterministic shuffling with fixed seed. Proposer caching (lines 279-287, 333-356) uses state root as key, ensuring consistency. Cryptographic binding: signing_root.go lines 174-193 (VerifyBlockSigningRoot) verify block signature against proposer public key retrieved from state. Block signing (ComputeDomainAndSign lines 57-83) requires proposer's secret key. Forgery requires breaking BLS signature scheme. Trust boundary tb-005/tb-009: Proposer identity cryptographically bound via signature, preventing repudiation attacks.
phase3.severity_assessment: Proposer selection is deterministic and cryptographically secure. BLS signature provides non-repudiation. No vulnerability to proposer identity spoofing or repudiation attacks.

BeaconProposerIndex computes the proposer from active validator indices and a seed derived from RANDAO with MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD delay. ProcessBlockHeader verifies the proposer_index field matches the expected proposer computed via helpers.BeaconProposerIndex. Block signature verification in VerifyBlockSignature ensures only the assigned proposer can sign the block.
phase1.abstract_state_space: State transitions: BeaconState -> Seed(epoch, DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER) -> ActiveValidatorIndices -> ComputeProposerIndex -> ValidatorIndex. The proposer selection is a pure function of (state, slot) with no external inputs. Access control boundary exists at ProcessBlockHeaderNoVerify line 107-113 where computed proposer index must match block's proposer_index field.

phase2.symbolic_constraints: For an unauthorized proposer to create a valid block: (1) Must compute valid proposer index from state, which is deterministic; (2) Block must pass ProcessBlockHeaderNoVerify check at line 111: proposerIndex != idx where idx = helpers.BeaconProposerIndex(ctx, beaconState); (3) Must produce valid BLS signature matching the assigned proposer's public key. Symbolic analysis shows no path where block.ProposerIndex can differ from computed idx and still pass validation.

phase3.proof_sketch: Invariant: ∀ valid_block, block.proposer_index = get_beacon_proposer_index(state). Proof: (1) ProcessBlockHeaderNoVerify explicitly checks this at line 107-113 and rejects if mismatch; (2) BeaconProposerIndex is deterministic from state via Seed(state, epoch, DomainBeaconProposer) + ActiveValidatorIndices + ComputeProposerIndex; (3) Seed incorporates RANDAO mix from epoch-1 via MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD; (4) VerifyBlockSignature at line 62 requires BLS signature from the assigned proposer's public key. The invariant is enforced at two layers: structural (proposer_index field) and cryptographic (BLS signature).
phase3.severity_assessment: Low severity confirmed as safe. The consensus layer correctly enforces proposer assignment through both deterministic computation and cryptographic verification. No elevation of privilege is possible.

phase1.summary: Proposer duty assignment is deterministic and non-repudiable. The assignment derives from public beacon state via PrecomputeProposerIndices which computes a lookahead array using Seed(state, epoch, DomainBeaconProposer). Any validator or verifier can independently compute the proposer for a given slot. BLS signatures on blocks provide non-repudiation: a valid block signature proves the assigned proposer created it.
phase1.abstract_state_space: Assignment computation: State -> get_seed(state, epoch, DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER) -> hash(seed || slot) -> compute_proposer_index(state, active_indices, seed_with_slot) -> ValidatorIndex. The computation is publicly verifiable and deterministic. Cache layer (proposerIndicesCache) stores computed assignments but does not affect determinism.

phase2.symbolic_constraints: For a validator to falsely deny proposer duty: They must claim the deterministic computation yielded a different result, but any verifier can recompute using the same beacon state. For a validator to falsely claim proposer duty: They must produce a block, but ProcessBlockHeader checks proposer_index against BeaconProposerIndex (line 107-113) and VerifyBlockSignature requires a valid BLS signature from the assigned proposer's key. Both attack paths are unreachable due to deterministic public computation and cryptographic binding.

phase3.proof_sketch: Invariant: Proposer assignment is non-repudiable and verifiable. Proof: (1) PrecomputeProposerIndices (beacon_committee.go:676-698) computes proposer for each slot using public state and deterministic seed; (2) Seed function (randao.go:22-38) uses public RANDAO mix from state.randao_mixes[epoch % EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR]; (3) ComputeProposerIndex (validators.go:398-441) is deterministic with inputs (state, active_indices, seed); (4) Any party can verify by recomputing: BeaconProposerIndexAtSlot returns the same result for all honest nodes; (5) BLS signature on block provides cryptographic proof of authorship by assigned proposer. The combination of public deterministic computation and BLS signatures prevents both denial and false claiming.
phase3.severity_assessment: Low severity confirmed as safe. Assignment integrity is maintained through deterministic public computation and cryptographic non-repudiation. No repudiation risk exists.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Is the MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD delay sufficient to prevent same-epoch randao manipulation of proposer assignments?

reachability.notes: A validator controlling multiple slots could attempt to bias the randao mix to manipulate future proposer assignments. The MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD provides a time buffer, but the attack is theoretically possible with sufficient validator share.

checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Review the implementation of MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD delay in proposer selection. 2. Identify all randao mix contribution points at epoch boundaries. 3. Analyze the proposer lookahead calculation to verify it correctly incorporates the seed lookahead delay. 4. Model the attack surface: calculate the validator stake percentage required to bias randao outcomes. 5. Verify that the delay between randao contribution and proposer assignment prevents same-epoch manipulation. 6. Test edge cases at epoch boundaries where timing assumptions may be violated. 7. Check for any code paths that could allow early revelation or late contribution of randao values.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-W1B10-53, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Primary Element: SG-006. This is an invariant property covering the consensus layer boundary between validators and the randao system. Bug bounty eligible - requires demonstration that MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD is insufficient with specific validator stake percentage.

phase1.summary: MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD provides sufficient delay to prevent same-epoch RANDAO manipulation of proposer assignments. The Seed function (randao.go:22-38) computes seed using RANDAO mix from epoch + EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1, effectively looking back 1 epoch. This means proposer selection for epoch N uses randao_mix from epoch N-1, preventing validators in epoch N from influencing their own proposer assignments.
phase1.abstract_state_space: Seed computation: lookAheadEpoch = epoch + EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1 = epoch + 65536 - 1 - 1 = epoch + 65534 (mod EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR). The modulo operation results in effective lookback: for epoch N, uses randao_mix[N-1]. Trust boundary tb-009 separates RANDAO contributors (untrusted validators) from proposer selection algorithm (consensus rules).

phase2.symbolic_constraints: For same-epoch RANDAO manipulation: Validator V proposing in epoch N must influence seed used for epoch N proposer selection. However, Seed(state, epoch=N, DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER) computes lookAheadEpoch = N + 65536 - 1 - 1 = N + 65534, then retrieves randao_mix[(N+65534) % 65536] = randao_mix[N-2 (for N>=2)]. ProcessRandao mixes block's randao_reveal into state.randao_mixes[currentEpoch % EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR]. RANDAO reveal in epoch N affects randao_mix[N], but epoch N proposer selection uses randao_mix[N-2]. The temporal gap of 2 epochs prevents same-epoch manipulation. Attack path is unreachable.

phase3.proof_sketch: Invariant: RANDAO contributions in epoch N cannot affect proposer assignments in epoch N. Proof: (1) Seed function at randao.go:25-26 computes lookAheadEpoch = epoch + EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1; (2) With MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD=1 and EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR=65536, for epoch N: lookAheadEpoch = N + 65536 - 1 - 1 = N + 65534; (3) RandaoMix retrieves state.randao_mixes[(N+65534) % 65536]; (4) For N < 65536, this equals randao_mixes[N+65534], but the modulo wraps, effectively creating a lookback; (5) Careful analysis: the formula ensures epoch N uses randao from epoch N-MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD-1; (6) ProcessRandao (randao.go:70) updates randao_mixes[currentEpoch % EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR] with current block's reveal; (7) Temporal separation of at least MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD=1 epoch prevents manipulation. The MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD delay is sufficient.
phase3.severity_assessment: Medium severity assessed as safe. The MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD=1 delay provides sufficient temporal separation to prevent same-epoch RANDAO manipulation. Trust boundary tb-009 integrity is maintained.

Verify that missing randao contributions are handled correctly (e.g., using a default value). 3. Check for replay protection on randao contributions. 4. phase1.summary: RANDAO reveals cannot be replayed (epoch-specific BLS signature prevents this), but withholding is a known protocol limitation. ProcessRandao at randao.go:30-53 verifies the RANDAO reveal is a valid BLS signature of the current epoch by the proposer. Replay protection: the signature is over the epoch number, so a RANDAO reveal for epoch N is invalid for epoch M ≠ N. Withholding: a proposer can choose not to propose, causing the default hash to be used, but this is mitigated by penalties for non-proposing and the MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD delay making the impact predictable.
phase1.abstract_state_space: RANDAO verification flow: Block contains RandaoReveal (BLS signature). ProcessRandao retrieves proposer pubkey, computes signing_root = compute_signing_root(currentEpoch, DOMAIN_RANDAO), and verifies BLS.Verify(proposer.pubkey, signing_root, randao_reveal). ProcessRandaoNoVerify XORs hash(randao_reveal) into state.randao_mixes[epoch % EPOCHS_PER_HISTORICAL_VECTOR]. Replay attack space: attacker tries to reuse reveal from epoch M in epoch N.
potential_violations: Withholding attack: proposer chooses not to produce block to avoid revealing RANDAO, causing predictable entropy source (known limitation, not exploitable due to lookahead).

phase2.symbolic_constraints: Replay attack: For RANDAO reveal R_M from epoch M to be accepted in epoch N ≠ M: (1) randaoSigningData computes buf = epoch N in little-endian (line 168); (2) signing_root = hash(SigningData{ObjectRoot: buf, Domain: DOMAIN_RANDAO}); (3) verifySignature checks BLS.Verify(proposer.pubkey, signing_root, R_M); (4) R_M is signature over epoch M, so verification fails for epoch N. Replay is unreachable. Withholding: Proposer in epoch N can skip proposing. If no block at slot S, no RANDAO reveal is mixed in. However, Seed for epoch N+2 is already determined by epoch N+1, so withholding in epoch N doesn't affect epoch N+2 assignments. Attack is conditional on withholding causing predictable randomness, but lookahead prevents this.
phase2.attack_path: Withholding scenario: Validator assigned to propose at slot S in epoch N decides not to publish block. Result: No RANDAO reveal mixed for that slot, state.randao_mixes[N] retains previous value. However, proposer assignments for epoch N+1 are already computed from epoch N-1's RANDAO mix (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD). Impact: minimal, as missing one slot's RANDAO contribution doesn't significantly reduce entropy, and the proposer loses block rewards.

phase3.proof_sketch: Invariant: RANDAO reveals cannot be replayed to influence proposer selection. Proof: (1) ProcessRandao at randao.go:39-47 calls randaoSigningData which encodes currentEpoch in the signing data (line 167-168); (2) BLS signature verification at line 45 checks sig.Verify(publicKey, signing_root) where signing_root includes the epoch; (3) A signature S_M valid for epoch M will fail verification for epoch N ≠ M because the signing_root differs; (4) Withholding is not exploitable for influencing proposer selection due to MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD: epoch N assignments use epoch N-1 RANDAO, so withholding in epoch N doesn't affect epoch N; (5) Known limitation: complete non-participation can make RANDAO predictable, but this requires majority validator collusion and is economically irrational due to lost rewards. The invariant holds for replay prevention; withholding is a documented limitation with minimal impact.
phase3.counterexample: Withholding is possible but not exploitable: a proposer can choose not to propose, but this doesn't allow influencing their own future proposer assignments due to the lookahead delay.
phase3.severity_assessment: Medium severity assessed as informational with caveats. Replay protection is strong (epoch-bound BLS signatures). Withholding is a known protocol limitation with minimal practical impact due to MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD delay and economic disincentives. No tampering vulnerability exists that allows targeted manipulation of proposer selection.

(4) This returns (activation_epoch <= epoch) AND (epoch < exit_epoch). (5) For exited validators: exit_epoch <= current_epoch = epoch. (6) Thus epoch < exit_epoch is false, validator excluded. When a validator is slashed via SlashValidator (validator.go:231-298), InitiateValidatorExit is called which sets exit_epoch to a future epoch. Until that exit_epoch arrives, a slashed validator CAN be selected as proposer. The slashed flag serves other purposes (e.g., preventing double-slashing, calculating penalties) but does not directly affect the active validator check.
phase1.abstract_state_space: Validator state includes (slashed: bool, exit_epoch: Epoch, activation_epoch: Epoch). Active check is purely epoch-based. A slashed validator remains in active set until exit_epoch is reached. State transition: slash event -> exit_epoch set to future value -> validator remains active for interim epochs -> exit_epoch reached -> validator becomes inactive.
potential_violations: Slashed validator can propose blocks between slashing time and exit_epoch

phase2.symbolic_constraints: For slashed validator to be selected as proposer: (1) validator.slashed = true, (2) validator.activation_epoch <= current_epoch, (3) current_epoch < validator.exit_epoch. When SlashValidator is called at epoch E, exit_epoch is set to E + exit_delay (typically 4-8 epochs). During epochs (E, E+exit_delay), the validator satisfies the active check despite being slashed.
phase2.attack_path: Scenario: Validator V is slashed at epoch 100. InitiateValidatorExit sets exit_epoch to 108. At epoch 105, V still passes IsActiveValidatorUsingTrie (100 <= 105 < 108 = true) and can be selected via ComputeProposerIndex. However, this is INTENDED spec behavior, not a vulnerability.

phase3.proof_sketch: Invariant (if interpreted as 'slashed validators cannot propose'): DOES NOT HOLD in implementation, but this matches Ethereum spec. The spec intentionally allows slashed validators to remain active until exit_epoch. Rationale: (1) Immediate removal would complicate validator set stability, (2) Exit queue management prevents sudden validator set changes, (3) Slashed validators face economic penalties making malicious proposals unprofitable. Evidence from code: IsActiveValidatorUsingTrie does not check slashed flag (validators.go:51-53). SlashValidator calls InitiateValidatorExit which sets future exit_epoch (validator.go:239).
phase3.counterexample: Validator slashed at epoch E with exit_epoch = E+8 can be selected as proposer at epoch E+4. However, this is spec-compliant.
phase3.severity_assessment: This is NOT a vulnerability but spec-compliant behavior. The Ethereum consensus spec intentionally allows slashed validators to remain in the active set until exit_epoch. The title's assertion that slashed validators 'cannot be selected' is technically incorrect - they CAN be selected until exited, but this is by design. No security risk as economic incentives prevent malicious behavior.

The validateDenebBeaconBlock function (validate_beacon_blocks.go:317-333) checks that len(commits) <= maxBlobsPerBlock via params.BeaconConfig().MaxBlobsPerBlock(slot), rejecting blocks that exceed this limit. P2P rate limiting is enforced via: (1) One block per slot per proposer via hasSeenBlockIndexSlot check, (2) libp2p RPC rate limiters in rate_limiter.go with configurable burst limits, (3) Gossip validation prevents duplicate processing.

Each proposer can submit at most 1 block per slot. Each block can contain at most MaxBlobsPerBlock commitments (6 for Deneb, 9 for Electra, configurable via BlobSchedule).

Even with valid credentials, a proposer can only submit 1 block per slot. Resource exhaustion via legitimate max-blob blocks is bounded by slot time (12 seconds) and network gossip limits.

phase3.proof_sketch: Invariant: P2P layer prevents resource exhaustion from excessive blob commitments. Proof sketch: (1) Per-block limit: validateDenebBeaconBlock enforces len(commits) <= MaxBlobsPerBlock(slot), rejecting violations (validate_beacon_blocks.go:326-331). (2) Per-proposer-slot limit: hasSeenBlockIndexSlot enforces one block per (slot, proposer_index), subsequent blocks ignored (validate_beacon_blocks.go:113-124). (3) Per-peer rate limiting: rate_limiter.go implements leaky bucket collectors for block requests with configurable limits (rate_limiter.go:38-108). (4) Signature verification: Only proposer with correct BLS key can create valid blocks (validate_beacon_blocks.go:296-298). (5) Gossip layer: libp2p gossipsub has built-in message deduplication and peer scoring. Combined, these mechanisms bound resource consumption: max rate = (slots per second) * MaxBlobsPerBlock ≈ (1/12) * 6-9 ≈ 0.5-0.75 blobs/sec for legitimate traffic. QED.
phase3.severity_assessment: The implementation provides defense-in-depth against blob-based resource exhaustion. Multiple layers of validation and rate limiting prevent both malicious flooding and accidental overload. Minor uncertainty (0.95 vs 1.0 confidence) stems from reliance on libp2p gossipsub implementation details for final layer of protection.

phase1.summary: P2P layer properly authenticates proposer identity via BLS signature verification. In validatePhase0Block (validate_beacon_blocks.go:285-314), the proposer signature is verified using blocks.VerifyBlockSignatureUsingCurrentFork against the proposer's public key from state. Rate limiting is per-proposer-slot via hasSeenBlockIndexSlot, not per-connection. A peer cannot forge proposer identity as it requires the proposer's BLS private key. Peer identity (libp2p peer ID) is separate from validator identity (BLS public key).
phase1.abstract_state_space: Authentication flow: (1) Block received from peer P with claimed proposer_index I, (2) State lookup: retrieve validator[I].public_key, (3) Signature verification: BLS.Verify(public_key, block_root, signature), (4) If valid: proposer authenticated as validator I, (5) Rate limit enforcement: track (slot, proposer_index) not (slot, peer_id). A malicious peer can send blocks claiming any proposer_index, but only valid signatures pass verification.

phase2.symbolic_constraints: For peer P to spoof proposer identity I: (1) Create block B with proposer_index = I, (2) Compute block_root = hash(B), (3) Generate valid signature S such that BLS.Verify(validator[I].pubkey, block_root, S) = true. Without validator I's private key, generating S is cryptographically infeasible (requires breaking BLS signature scheme). If P has I's private key, they ARE proposer I, not a spoof. Rate limiting tracks (slot, proposer_index) so even if P controls multiple libp2p identities, they cannot bypass the one-block-per-slot-per-proposer limit.

phase3.proof_sketch: Invariant: Proposer identity cannot be spoofed for rate-limiting bypass. Proof: (1) Proposer authentication: VerifyBlockSignatureUsingCurrentFork (signature.go:101-120) verifies BLS signature against proposer public key from state. (2) BLS security: Breaking BLS signatures is computationally infeasible under standard cryptographic assumptions. (3) Rate limiting anchor: hasSeenBlockIndexSlot uses (slot, proposer_index) tuple as key (validate_beacon_blocks.go:410-411), independent of peer identity. (4) Signature verification precedes rate limit enforcement in early blocks (validate_beacon_blocks.go:180-183, 198-201). (5) Even if attacker controls multiple peer IDs, they cannot create multiple valid signatures for the same proposer_index without the private key. (6) If attacker HAS the private key, they are the legitimate proposer. (7) Therefore, rate limiting correctly tracks proposer identity, not peer identity. QED.
phase3.severity_assessment: Proposer identity authentication is cryptographically sound via BLS signatures. Rate limiting correctly operates on authenticated proposer identity, not spoofable peer identity. No vulnerability detected.
